newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to budget $293 mln in local government aid.
newsitem.headline: Israel to budget $293 mln in local government aid.

text.p: The Israeli government will pay one billion shekels ($293.3 million) over three years to cover the budget deficits of indebted local municipalities, the Treasury said on Friday.
The Treasury will pay 300 million shekels in 1997, half of which has already been budgeted in fiscal 1997, 500 million shekels in 1998, and 200 million in 1999.
The sources said local governments had accepted Treasury terms requiring them to undertake measures to balance their budgets, abolish unauthorised wage agreements and cut costs.
"The terms are a precondition for receiving any future aid," one Treasury source said.

The agreement put an end to a three-week strike by local governments, who had demanded an aid package from the central government including the rescheduling of eight billion shekels in debt and the provision of four billion shekels in actual aid.
